r:Description.r:Content: Usage: Title of the Study. If additional titles are required in other languages, use the parTitl element
Usage: Language of the study title. ISO 639-1 codes are strongly encouraged to be used.

Usage: Title of the Study in additional languages other than the 'titl' element. It is preferable to include this element to hold an English version of the title if the 'titl' element is not in English.
Required: Mandatory if 'parTitl' element is present
Usage: Language of the translated study title. ISO 639-1 codes are strongly encouraged to be used.

Usage: The content of this element serves two purposes. It is used both for the PID and for the study/archival number given by the SP. These two cases have different specifications. IDNo in the sense of study number is optional. PID is mandatory
Usage: Language is recommended when the agency attribute contains an organisation name, for example, in the context of 'IDNo' being used to display the internal study number

Usage: Agency responsible for the identifier of the study. If you are using IDNo for a Persistent Identifer, value should be one of https://vocabularies.cessda.eu/vocabulary/CessdaPersistentIdentifierTypes i.e. ARK or DOI or Handle or URN

Usage: Language of the study description page at the SP website (there can be multiple 'holding' elements for study description pages in different languages. ISO 639-1 codes are strongly encouraged to be used.
Usage: This is the document the metadata refers to, i.e. the URL of the study description page at the SP website.
Usage: Principal investigator Person OR Institution

Usage: Language of the Organisation name, which may be the contents of the AuthEnty element or the affiliation attribute if AuthEnty specifies a person. ISO 639-1 codes codes are strongly encouraged to be used.
Usage: If AuthEnty is a person, the organisational affiliation of that person
Usage: The persistent identifier (PID) of the principal investigator/creator or the PID of the affiliation of the principal investigator/creator e.g. 0000-0002-7668-5427 (ORCID) or 033003e23 (ROR)
Required: Mandatory if '..../ddi:AuthEnty/ddi:ExtLink' element is present.
Usage: The URL of the PID. Please note, that the URI attribute is mandatory for the ExtLink element due to the DDI-C specification.

Usage: The role of the PID. Must be used when the PID refers to the affiliation and in this case the attribute value must be "affiliation-PID". If the PID refers to the PI or creator, it is recommended to use value "PID" for this field
Usage: The type of the PID. If the PID is documented, the type of the PID should be documented, too.
Usage: Agency which provided the funding.
Usage: Language of the name of the agency which provided the funding. ISO 639-1 codes are strongly encouraged to be used.

Usage: The identification code of the grant or other monetary award which provided funding for the Study. If you know that the funder is included in the OpenAire list of Funders, see the instructions for grantNo syntax here: https://guidelines.openaire.eu/en/latest/data/field_contributor.html#nameidentifier-ma-o . Indicate the appropriate agency using the "agency" attribute. If different funding agencies sponsored different stages of the production process, use the "role" attribute to distinguish the grant numbers.
Usage: Language of the name of the agency which provided the funding. ISO 639-1 codes are strongly encouraged to be used.
Usage: Agency which provided the funding.
Usage: The element should contain the name of the organisation who has published the metadata for the harvested study description. This is usually the SP.
Usage: Language of the organisation name. ISO codes are strongly encouraged to be used.
Usage: Abbreviated form of the Publisher name e.g. 'UKDA' for 'UK Data Archive'
Usage: URI to the series description page in the SPs web page
Usage: Language of the whole serStmt OR the URI to the series description page in the SPs web page. ISO 639-1 codes are strongly encouraged to be used.
Usage: The name of the series.
Required: Mandatory if 'serName' element is present.
Usage: Language of the name of the series. ISO 639-1 codes are strongly encouraged to be used.
Usage: The description of the series.
Required: Mandatory if 'serInfo' element is present.
Usage: Language of the description of the series. ISO 639-1 codes are strongly encouraged to be used.
Usage: Keyword for the study in the local language.
Required: Mandatory if 'keyword' element is present
Usage: Language of the keyword. ISO 639-1 codes are strongly encouraged to be used.
Usage: The name of the used vocabulary. If possible, use "ELSST" (regardless of language) but other vocabularies are also permitted.
Usage: Optional but note that if vocab="ELSST", then use "https://elsst.cessda.eu/id/" here.

Usage: Subject classifcation term for the study in the local language. Use descriptive terms from https://vocabularies.cessda.eu/vocabulary/TopicClassification if possible but other vocabularies are permitted.
Required: Mandatory if 'topcClas' element is present
Usage: Language of the subject classification term. ISO 639-1 codes are strongly encouraged to be used.
Usage: The name of the used vocabulary. If possible, use "CESSDA Topic Classification" (regardless of language) but other vocabularies are also permitted.

Usage: Use the URI of the CV version that is being used based on the pattern "https://vocabularies.cessda.eu/urn/urn:ddi:int.cessda.cv:TopicClassification:[version number]" For example, for version 4.2.2 of CESSDA Topic Classification, use "https://vocabularies.cessda.eu/urn/urn:ddi:int.cessda.cv:TopicClassification:4.2.2"
Usage: This is the free text expression of the collection period. This element may be empty.
Usage: Language of the free text expression of the collection period. ISO 639-1 codes are strongly encouraged to be used.
Usage: Either 'start', 'end' or 'single' to indicate the type of date attribute
Usage: Ideally YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ format, but can accept YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM or YYYY as date attribute. If there are multiple end dates, use the last.
Usage: The cycle/wave of the data collection
Usage: Countries relevant to the study area
Required: Mandatory if 'nation' element is present
Usage: Language of the country label. ISO 639-1 codes are strongly encouraged to be used.
Usage: Use this attribute only if the country in the 'nation' element has an ISO 3166-1 2-letter code.
Usage: Contains the Analysis Unit CV item in the local language.
Required: Mandatory if 'anlyUnit' element is present
Usage: Language of the Analysis Unit CV item. ISO 639-1 codes are strongly encouraged to be used.

Analysis Unit Controlled Vocabulary "Code value" that is the same across languages. e.g if the "anlyUnit" element is 'Kotitalous' for Finnish, the "concept" element is 'Household'. See example at https://vocabularies.cessda.eu/urn/urn:ddi:int.ddi.cv:AnalysisUnit.
Usage: Use the string "DDI Analysis Unit" regardless of language.

Usage: The URL of the CV version that is being used e.g. https://vocabularies.cessda.eu/urn/urn:ddi:int.ddi.cv:AnalysisUnit:2.1.3 or https://vocabularies.cessda.eu/v2/vocabularies/AnalysisUnit/1.0.0?languageVersion=en-1.0.0
Usage: Description of population or other elements studied or measured (freetext).
Required: Mandatory if 'universe' element is present.
Usage: Language of the Universe item. ISO 639-1 codes are strongly encouraged to be used.

Usage: The default value is "true" in DDI-L. The description statement of a universe is generally stated in inclusive terms such as "All persons residing in Europe". Occasionally a universe is defined by what it excludes, i.e., "All persons residing in Europe except for those residing on U.S. Military bases". In this case the value would be changed to "false". In DDI-C, attribute clusion states the inclusion/exclusion with values "I" and "E" respectively.
Usage: Contains the Time Method CV item in the local language
Required: Mandatory if 'timeMeth' element is present
Usage: Language of the Time Method CV item. ISO 639-1 codes are strongly encouraged to be used.

Usage: Time Method Controlled Vocabulary "Code value" that is the same across languages. e.g if the 'timeMeth' element is 'Pitkittäisaineisto' for Finnish, the 'concept' element is 'Longitudinal'. See example at https://vocabularies.cessda.eu/urn/urn:ddi:int.ddi.cv:TimeMethod
Usage: Use the string "DDI Time Method" regardless of language.

Usage: The URL of the CV version that is being used e.g. https://vocabularies.cessda.eu/urn/urn:ddi:int.ddi.cv:TimeMethod:1.2.3 or https://vocabularies.cessda.eu/v2/vocabularies/TimeMethod/1.2.0?languageVersion=en-1.2.0
Usage: Contains the Sampling Procedure CV item in the local language and/or a freetext description in the local language
Required: Mandatory if 'sampProc' element is present
Usage: Language of the Sampling Procedure CV item or freetext description. ISO 639-1 codes are strongly encouraged to be used.

Usage: Sampling Procedure Controlled Vocabulary "Code value" that is the same across languages. e.g if the 'sampProc' element is 'Todennäköisyysotanta' for Finnish, the 'concept' element is 'Probability'. See example at https://vocabularies.cessda.eu/urn/urn:ddi:int.ddi.cv:SamplingProcedure
Usage: Use the string "DDI Sampling Procedure" regardless of language.

Usage: The URL of the CV version that is being used e.g. https://vocabularies.cessda.eu/urn/urn:ddi:int.ddi.cv:SamplingProcedure:2.0.2 or https://vocabularies.cessda.eu/v2/vocabularies/SamplingProcedure/1.1.0?languageVersion=en-1.1.0
Usage: Contains the Mode of Collection CV item in the local language.
Required: Mandatory if 'collMode' element is present
Usage: Language of the Mode of Collection CV item. ISO 639-1 codes are strongly encouraged to be used.

Usage: Mode of Collection Controlled Vocabulary "Code value" that is the same across languages. e.g if the 'collMode' element is 'Haastattelu' for Finnish, the 'concept' element is 'Interview'. See example at https://vocabularies.cessda.eu/urn/urn:ddi:int.ddi.cv:ModeOfCollection
Usage: Use the string "DDI Mode of Collection" regardless of language.

Usage: The URL of the CV version that is being used e.g https://vocabularies.cessda.eu/urn/urn:ddi:int.ddi.cv:ModeOfCollection:5.0.1 or https://vocabularies.cessda.eu/v2/vocabularies/ModeOfCollection/3.0.0?languageVersion=en-3.0.0
Usage: Contains the Type of Instrument CV item in the local language.
Required: Mandatory if 'resInstru' element is present
Usage: Language of the Type of Instrument CV item. ISO 639-1 codes are strongly encouraged to be used.

Usage: the Type of Instrument Controlled Vocabulary "Code value" that is the same across languages. e.g if the 'resInstru' element is 'Lomake' for Finnish, the 'concept' element is 'Questionnaire'. See example at https://vocabularies.cessda.eu/urn/urn:ddi:int.ddi.cv:TypeOfInstrument:1.1.2
Usage: Use the string "DDI Type of Instrument" regardless of language.

Usage: The URL of the CV version that is being used e.g. https://vocabularies.cessda.eu/urn/urn:ddi:int.ddi.cv:TypeOfInstrument:1.1.2 or https://vocabularies.cessda.eu/v2/vocabularies/TypeOfInstrument/1.1.0?languageVersion=en-1.1.0

Usage: Refers to any information relating to the access and use conditions of data that the SP wants to send. SPs need to concatenate the information for 'restrctn' the way they want it to appear in the EQB, if they use data from different elements e.g.specPerm, restrctn, avlStatus etc.
Usage: Language of the Access statement. ISO 639-1 codes are strongly encouraged to be used.

Usage: Controlled description of the data access (open access vs. restricted access). EQB will use the COAR Access Rights vocabulary https://vocabularies.coar-repositories.org/access_rights/. Only the codes "restricted access" and "open access" will be used.
Usage: When the conditions element is used for vocabulary 'COAR Access Right Vocabulary', then use this vocabulary name 'COAR Access Right Vocabulary' in this field.
Usage: The language of the content of the element. ISO 639-1 codes are strongly encouraged to be used
Usage: The text for requiring the data user to inform the archive of their data usage.
Usage: The language of the content of the element. ISO 639-1 codes are strongly encouraged to be used
Usage: The material related to the study description
Usage: The title of the material related to the study description
Usage: The language of the content of the element. ISO 639-1 codes are strongly encouraged to be used
Required: Required: Mandatory if '//ddi:fileTxt/ddi:fileName' is present
Usage: The language of the content of the element. ISO 639-1 codes are strongly encouraged to be used
Usage: The ID of the variable group
Usage: Type of the variable group.
Usage: Identifiers of the variables belonging to this variable group.
Usage: The label of the variable group
Required: Mandatory if '//ddi:varGrp/ddi:labl' element is present.
Usage: The language of the content of the element. ISO 639-1 codes are strongly encouraged to be used
Usage: The Identifier of the variable
Usage: The name of the variable.
Usage: The indicator if the variable is weight ('wgt') or not ('not-wgt').
Usage: The file name identifiers of the files containing this variable
Usage: The label of the variable.
Required: Mandatory if '//ddi:var/ddi:labl' element is present
Usage: The language of the content of the element. ISO 639-1 codes are strongly encouraged to be used
Usage: The prequestion text appearing before the actual question text
Required: Mandatory if '//ddi:qstn/ddi:preQTxt' element is present.
Usage: The language of the content of the element. ISO 639-1 codes are strongly encouraged to be used
Usage: The literal question item text.
Required: Mandatory if '//ddi:qstn/ddi:qstnLit' element is present.
Usage: The language of the content of the element. ISO 639-1 codes are strongly encouraged to be used
Usage: The postquestion text appearing after the actual question text
Required: Mandatory if '//ddi:qstn/ddi:postQTxt' element is present.
Usage: The language of the content of the element. ISO 639-1 codes are strongly encouraged to be used
Usage: The instructions for the interviewer.
Required: Mandatory if '//ddi:qstn/ddi:ivuInstr' element is present.
Usage: The language of the content of the element. ISO 639-1 codes are strongly encouraged to be used
Usage: The type (integer/real) of individual valid value
Usage: The type (integer/real) of values in the range of valid values
Usage: The lowest value in the range of valid values
Usage: The highest value in the range of valid values
Usage: The type (integer/real) of individual invalid value
Usage: The type (integer/real) of values in the range of invalid values
Usage: The lowest value in the range of invalid values
Usage: The highest value in the range of invalid values
Usage: The value of the statistical measure
Usage: The type of statistical measure: minimum, maximum, mean, standard deviation, median, mode, valid cases or invalid cases.
Usage: This element serves two use cases: 1) Providing additional information about the variable, 2) Describing the variable when it is not derived from a question.
Required: Mandatory if '//ddi:var/ddi:txt' element is present.
Usage: The language of the content of the element. ISO 639-1 codes are strongly encouraged to be used
Usage: The indicator if the category represents a missing value ('Y') or not ('N').
Usage: The value related to the category.
Usage: The label of the category
Required: Mandatory if '//ddi:catgry/ddi:labl' element is present.
Usage: The language of the content of the element. ISO 639-1 codes are strongly encouraged to be used
Usage: The value of the statistical measure for the category.
Usage: The type of the statistical measure for the category e.g. 'freq' for frequency
Usage: The concept related to the variable.
Required: Mandatory if '//ddi:var/ddi:concept' element is present.
Usage: The language of the content of the element. ISO 639-1 codes are strongly encouraged to be used
